Romanovskaya

Astronomer · INASAN, Moscow

I study the chemical composition of stars from high-resolution spectra, focusing on magnetic chemically peculiar, normal, and metallic-line (Am) stars, as well as binary systems. I also use machine-learning methods in my work on binary stars.

About me

I am an astrophysicist working on stellar atmospheres, high-resolution spectroscopy, and chemical peculiarities in stars. My main research interests include magnetic chemically peculiar Ap/Bp stars, metallic-line Am/Fm stars, normal O–B–A–F stars, and spectroscopic binary systems.

I study how chemical anomalies, magnetic fields, stellar rotation, and binarity affect observed spectra and the determination of stellar atmospheric parameters. More recently, I have been developing and applying machine-learning methods to estimate the parameters of both components of spectroscopic binary stars from composite spectra.

Research topics

A short overview of the directions I work on, with illustrative figures.

01

Chemical composition of stars

Determining detailed elemental abundances from high-resolution stellar spectra, line by line.

spectroscopyabundances
02

Magnetic chemically peculiar stars

Studying strong magnetic fields and anomalous abundances through Zeeman-split spectral lines.

magnetismCP stars
03

Normal & metallic-line (Am) stars

Comparing line strengths and abundances of Am and normal A-type stars to probe their atmospheres.

Am starsatmospheres
04

Binary stars & machine learning

Analysing binary systems from spectra and light curves, using machine-learning methods to speed up the work.
